Check a volatility break and place it in the sample

Source: R/volatility_break.R
check_volatility_break.Rd

Validates the volatility break of Lenza and Primiceri (2022) and returns the two fields a model carries for it, or NULL when no break was asked for.

Usage

check_volatility_break(volatility_break, volatility_scales, y, algorithm)

Arguments

volatility_break

the first period of the break as a date of the data, c(year, period) such as c(2020, 3), or a single time such as 2020. NULL for no break.

volatility_scales

a whole number of at least one, how many periods from the break on get a scale of their own before the excess decays.

y

the endogenous series of the estimation sample, whose time the date is looked up in.

algorithm

the sampler the model would be estimated with.

Value

A named list with the integer elements volatility_break and volatility_scales, or NULL.

Details

create_bvarmodel and create_bvecmodel call this, and it is exported so that a package building its own models – the sub-models of a global model in bgvars among them – validates a break the same way rather than repeating the arithmetic. The break is given as a date and kept as the period of y it falls on, counted from one, which is what /model/volatility_break of a model file holds and what the sampler reads.

It is refused for every algorithm but the two constant coefficient Wishart samplers, VarNormalWishart and VecNormalWishart, which are the ones that scale the error covariance from a known period on. A break outside the estimation sample is refused as well: the periods after it are what estimate its size.

References

Lenza, M. and Primiceri, G. E. (2022). How to estimate a vector autoregression after March 2020. Journal of Applied Econometrics, 37(4), 688–699.
